members.working:
Identify the product containing the named element in each reaction and determine its magnetic properties (diamagnetic vs paramagnetic). Diamagnetic species have all electrons paired. Typical ionic/complex products:
(i) CoCl₂ + NH₃ (excess) → Co(III) complex (e.g., [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺) low-spin d⁶ → all electrons paired → diamagnetic.
(ii) Cu(OH)₂ heated → Cu(OH)₂ decomposes to CuO (Cu²⁺ d⁹) → one unpaired electron → paramagnetic.
(iii) CuSO₄ + excess KI → CuI precipitate (Cu⁺ d¹⁰) → all paired → diamagnetic.
(iv) Co²⁺ + CH₃COOH + excess KNO₂ → likely Co(III) nitrite complex (Co³⁺ d⁶ low-spin) → diamagnetic.
(v) Ni²⁺ + NH₄OH + H₂S → Ni(OH)₂ or NiS precipitate; Ni²⁺ d⁸ typically paramagnetic (high-spin) → paramagnetic.
(vi) NH₃ + O₂ burning → N₂ formed (N≡N) → diamagnetic.
(vii) Zn(NO₃)₂ heated → ZnO (Zn²⁺ d¹⁰) → diamagnetic.
Thus diamagnetic products: (i), (iii), (iv), (vi), (vii) = 5 reactions.
Answer integer 5.
